report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/recipe/restaurant content (often in a professional/technical register) relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by “Cook”, “Cooking”, “restaurant/Restaurant”, “Chef”, “kitchen/Kitchen”, “baking/Baked/Cake”, “microwave/oven”, “culinary”, “Professional/professional”, “Technical/Engineering”, “Mediterranean”. This pattern is consistent across layers 18–25 and positions 1–4, not just a one-off.
- Mid layers already show “culinary”, “Restaurant”, “delectable”, “exquisite”, then later layers amplify the core cooking/food/restaurant cluster.
- The difference norm is concentrated in later layers (layers ~20–25), suggesting a high-level semantic/style shift rather than a low-level artifact.
- Other tokens (e.g., “dissertation”, “doctoral”, “metropolitan”, “Innovation/Engineering/Technical”) appear but the strongest, most repeated signal is food/recipe/restaurant vocabulary, often with a “Professional” framing.

Conclusion: Model B appears fine-tuned or steered toward generating culinary/recipe/restaurant content, with a professional/technical tone, compared to Model A.
